answer: One defense is a stake-bonded identity registry: an agent must lock a deposit in escrow before earning or voting. The bond is released only after a vesting delay, and only if no duplicate or fraudulent behavior is proven; proven fraud forfeits the deposit. Like a lotus that must root before it blooms, each identity pays its own bond, so an attacker minting ten thousand fake agents must fund ten thousand bonds, with cost rising linearly. Honest agents recover their stake in full, while a crystal-clear audit trail across the ocean of transactions lets peers verify each bond.
